clue.text: Major policy for a minor state

definitions.text: Major policy for a minor state

parts.words: Major policy for a minor state
parts.note: a big principle of European Union government that leaves decisions to the smaller, more local level wherever possible

explanation.surface: A small country's grand political strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' and 'minor' play off each other: the principle is that power should sit with the lowest, most local tier, a key idea in the EU's Maastricht Treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: The principle holds that a central authority should handle only what local bodies cannot, so it is a policy favouring lesser states and tiers.

clue.text: Propose dispersing guests around the Grand

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation, holding it inside them
guests who disperse scatter about, so the letters of this word are scattered into a new order

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone recommends sending the guests away from the Grand Hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersing' rearranges GUESTS into SUGEST, and 'around' puts G inside it after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea for consideration is a synonym of offering it as a proposal.

clue.text: Riverside where deposits may accumulate

definitions.meaning: the sloping ground beside a river
a financial institution holding savings, or the river edge where silt is laid down

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the edge of a river and the institution that keeps customers' money.

clue.text: Cranky offer which brings nobody any good

definitions.text: Cranky offer which brings nobody any good

parts.words: Cranky offer which brings nobody any good
parts.note: a nod to the proverb about a harmful breeze that benefits no one, with 'Cranky offer' read as a sick puff of air

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered proposal that benefits no one.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'It's an ill wind that blows nobody any good', meaning almost any misfortune benefits someone; the clue plays on the literal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial phrase describes an unlucky event, a breeze so bad it helps no one at all.

clue.text: Full understanding is now not far off

definitions.meaning: deep perception or grasp of a matter
as a phrase, visible and close at hand, as a goal that is near

explanation.definitionFit: Clear perception of a matter is one sense; read as two words, it means visible and approaching.

clue.text: It crops up in the field when yellow

definitions.text: It crops up in the field when yellow

parts.words: It crops up in the field when yellow
parts.note: an oilseed crop whose flowering fields turn bright yellow in spring, with 'crops up' punning on farming

explanation.surface: Something appears in a meadow once it turns yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crops up' sounds like 'appears' but points to a farm crop; oilseed fields are a familiar vivid yellow in the British countryside in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilseed is a field crop of the cabbage family, grown widely and flowering bright yellow.

clue.text: If not too busy you may find it on watch

definitions.text: If not too busy you may find it on watch

parts.words: If not too busy you may find it on watch
parts.note: a wristwatch shows the hour, and a person with leisure is said to have spare hours for something

explanation.surface: A sentry with a quiet shift can find something while on guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on watch' suggests sentry duty but means on a wristwatch; someone not busy 'has the time' for you.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch's face shows the current hour, and having free hours is the idiom for being available.

clue.text: How to look smart and urge your case

definitions.meaning: ironing a jacket and trousers gives a neat appearance
to push a petition or courtship insistently

explanation.definitionFit: Literally ironing clothes makes you smart; figuratively a suit is a plea, and pressing it means urging it.

clue.text: Didn't start on time so wasn't relieved from duty

definitions.meaning: a racehorse that fails to break when the race begins is stranded at the starting point
a sentry abandoned at a station without a replacement

explanation.definitionFit: The racing idiom means being slow away at the start; literally it is a guard left standing at a post.

clue.text: True spirit in the heart of a queen

indicators.note: the spirit sits in the middle of the word for true, placed at its heart

parts.note: real means genuine or true
gin is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: A monarch's sincere spirit lies deep within her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' reads as soul or character but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means queenly, pertaining to a sovereign lady, from the Latin for queen.

clue.text: Highest army technicians go to dine

parts.note: to sup is to eat an evening meal
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, the British Army's technical corps

explanation.surface: Top military engineers head off for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank or degree, the topmost.

clue.text: One looks or looks on

parts.note: a person who sees, especially one who peers on into the future as a prophet

explanation.surface: A person watches, or merely spectates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks on' suggests a bystander, but here it means looking onward into what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or visionary is one who sees what lies ahead.

clue.text: Being drunk. And how!

indicators.note: a drunken word staggers about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Being intoxicated, and very much so!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a drinking spree, an extreme way of being drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree of heavy drinking is the classic case of getting thoroughly intoxicated.

clue.text: Roll — that's what ships do if they roll

definitions.meaning: a register or roster of names

definitions.text: what ships do if they roll
definitions.meaning: a vessel tilting over to one side

explanation.definitionFit: A roll of names is a register, and a vessel heeling over to one side is said to do this.

clue.text: Frown at a complaining cow

definitions.meaning: to scowl or look sullen
one that lows, as a mooing beast does

explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is one sense (also spelt lour); a bovine that moos is one that lows.

clue.text: Rumba cast a shadow

indicators.note: letters cast about land in a new order, as dice are thrown

explanation.surface: A Latin dance throws a dark shape on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the verb of throwing a shadow but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the darkest central part of a shadow, as in an eclipse.

clue.text: Suffering from hypothermal exposure, and unconscious

definitions.meaning: literally outside in freezing weather
knocked senseless

explanation.definitionFit: Literally left outdoors in the chill; idiomatically knocked senseless.

clue.text: Storm caused by Strasbourg politician during trial

indicators.note: the politician comes during the trial, inside it

parts.note: a test is a trial
a European MP, E plus MP, one who sits in the parliament at Strasbourg

explanation.surface: A Euro-politician's trial sparks an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: The politician is written E plus MP rather than the usual MEP, so the letters slot in after the first T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm.

clue.text: A humpty dumpty backroom boy

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme character is an egg with a face, while a backroom boy is a brainy behind-the-scenes expert

explanation.walkthrough: Humpty Dumpty is the egg-shaped figure of a nursery rhyme; 'backroom boy' is British for a technical expert working out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A highbrow intellectual is mocked by likening their domed head to an egg.

clue.text: Dutch equivalent of our sovereign given to trade association

indicators.note: the sovereign is given to the association, attached on after it

parts.note: a guild is a medieval association of craftsmen or merchants
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Dutch counterpart of a British coin is handed to a trade body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the gold coin the definition compares, but in the wordplay it is the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilder was the Netherlands' currency unit before the euro, its counterpart to the British pound.

clue.text: What autocrats do to their, secretaries

definitions.text: What autocrats do to their, secretaries

parts.words: What autocrats do to their, secretaries
parts.note: tyrants order everyone about, and bosses speak letters aloud to typists to take down

explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits two senses: what autocrats do (give orders) and what is done to secretaries (letters spoken for typing).
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrants lay down the law, and executives speak letters for a typist to record.

clue.text: As a result of being qualified for the next round

definitions.meaning: by means of or owing to
having advanced in a competition

explanation.definitionFit: It means owing to, and in sport it means having advanced to the following stage.

clue.text: Famous London street for everyone

definitions.meaning: the ceremonial avenue running from Buckingham Palace to Admiralty Arch
as two words, all those people

explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial avenue by Buckingham Palace; split differently, it means every one of those people.

clue.text: More competent in America are they who take a great interest

definitions.text: they who take a great interest

indicators.note: the comparative goes in the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: US is the United States
surer means more sure, more assured or capable

explanation.surface: Keener Americans take a strong interest in things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a great interest' sounds like curiosity but means charging exorbitant interest on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneylenders charging extortionate rates on loans collect a great deal of interest.

clue.text: Jump over a builder's disposal bin

definitions.meaning: to leap or pass over something
the large open rubbish container left outside building works

explanation.definitionFit: To hop past something is one sense; the British word for a large rubbish container is the other.

clue.text: Common wages paid to common prison warder

definitions.meaning: a slang word for salary
a slang word for a jailer

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the same word means a salary and a jail guard.

clue.text: Fit of the sulks displayed by Richard III!

definitions.meaning: in British idiom, to have this is to be in a bad mood
the king is traditionally shown as a hunchback

explanation.definitionFit: 'Having the hump' is British for sulking; the king is famously portrayed with a crooked back.

clue.text: Bleats from a colonial master

definitions.meaning: sheep's cries
a South African word for a boss or white master

explanation.definitionFit: Sheep's cries are one sense; the Afrikaans-derived word for a boss is the other.

clue.text: Does it teach only 10 letters of the alphabet?

definitions.text: Does it teach only 10 letters of the alphabet?

parts.words: Does it teach only 10 letters of the alphabet?
parts.note: split as '...', the name covers just ten letters: E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N

explanation.surface: A school with a very short reading syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the famous English public school near Windsor; split into three bits it reads E to N.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a place that teaches, and this famous one's name spells a short span of the alphabet.

clue.text: State of North America attached to the sub-continent

indicators.note: the abbreviation is attached on after the country

parts.note: India is the Indian sub-continent

explanation.surface: A North American region joined to South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Innocent of any cultural attainment?

parts.note: 'Innocent' is the plain sense, guileless; the rest reads the word as lacking all art

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading: without art, as well as simple and guileless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naive and without guile is the plain sense; split, it means devoid of artistry.

clue.text: Telephone mix up leads to misunderstanding

definitions.meaning: a fault connecting two calls together
a failure to communicate

explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard fault joining calls is the literal sense; figuratively it is two people talking at cross purposes.
